title: An explicit computable transcendental counterexample for Erdős Problem #206
abstract: A Lean formalization of a deterministic rational nested-interval construction defining a particular transcendental real x in (1/4,1/3). For this x, no strictly increasing infinite sequence of positive integer denominators is optimal among all distinct-denominator strict Egyptian underapproximations at every order from any finite starting order onward. The formalization includes the fully specified terminating construction, all prefix and polynomial enumerations, a total executable rational approximation function, and the error bound |x-q_n| <= 2^(-n-1) for every n >= 0. It also proves attainment of the best finite underapproximation values. The independent Palomar statement quantifies directly over all sequences and all competing positive increasing lists. This is a specific effective example; the measure-zero and prior existence results are not claimed as new.
